definitions.explanation: A set phrase said before eating to express gratitude for the food. Literally means 'I humbly receive.'

examples.english: I humbly receive this food. (said before eating)

examples.japanese: おいしそう！いただきます！
{手|て}を{合|あ}わせていただきます。
examples.english: I put my hands together and say 'itadakimasu.'

examples.japanese: {母|はは}が「いただきます」と{言|い}って、{食|た}べ{始|はじ}めました。
examples.english: My mother said 'itadakimasu' and started eating.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{食事|しょくじ}の{前|まえ}に「いただきます」と{言|い}う{習慣|しゅうかん}があります。
examples.english: In Japan, there is a custom of saying 'itadakimasu' before meals.

notes: いただきます is said before eating any meal, expressing gratitude to those who prepared the food, the farmers, and all living things that gave their life for the meal. It's a fundamental Japanese custom. Children are taught this phrase from a young age. The verb いただく is the humble form of もらう (to receive).
